content:
Princess Diana's brother Charles Spencer has publicly addressed the rift between Princes William and Harry.

Speaking to the BBC, Spencer said: "I think there's a perception in the media that I'm on Harry's side. But I'm actually on the side of my late sister's two boys, both of them." The interview aired on Sunday to coincide with the release of his new book about Diana, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister."

The historian added: "Whichever of the two needs me, I'll support them equally. I would never take sides with either camp; I only hope to play a friendly role."

Discussing the broken relationship between Harry and William, Spencer said things have "reached this point" and that "there are many reasons on both sides."

He shared: "I hope one day it can be resolved, but I don't know everything. I'm certainly not privy to the details, so if I got any more involved, I'd feel I was overstepping. I'll just say that, naturally, a mother would want her two boys to be happy and to love each other."

In a separate interview with People magazine, Spencer touched on another topic of concern to royal fans: when he informed the two princes about the book.

Spencer said: "I told them at the same time. What I can say is that one of them... well, all four of us together [William, Harry, and Spencer's two sisters, Sarah and Jane], I told all of them at the same time." He also said: "I can say Harry had absolutely no problem with it."

He shared: "He [Harry] said he hoped there was nothing embarrassing about him in the book. I said 'no.' I think they were both worried about what I might write." He added that the book "basically ends with Diana's death in 1997."

He also said: "But I can put their minds at rest — they do appear in the book, of course, but only as examples of two little boys who had the most amazing mother. I had absolutely no intention of invading their privacy."

Spencer's book was published on Tuesday, ahead of the 30th anniversary of Diana's death — 31 August 1997.
